15:32 Local Time, 09:32 GMT, 15:02 IST: And they are walking off. The light an issue. Chase appreciates his players by clapping them. West Indies well on top here even though this is a good partnership between Jaker Ali and Nayeem Hasan. They have arrested the fall of wickets with dogged defence and at times attack. Nayeem though had to review to save himself from being LBW after being given out. Chase and Warrican outstanding for West Indies. They have bowled superbly in tandem and richly deserved their wickets. The ball has started to turn and Bangladesh will try to eke out as many as they can.

16:33 Local Time, 10:33 GMT, 16:03 IST: The surface deteriorated rapidly on the moving day and the spinners from both sides ruled the roost on it - as many as 12 wickets fell today. Chanderpaul’s gritty fifty and 40s from Chase and Greaves were pivotal in West Indies getting close to Bangladesh’s 272 but the hosts still gained a slender 27-run lead. Nayeem Hasan stood out as he sliced through the lower order to finish with a 4-fer. In response, Shamar got rid of Tanzid for a duck. A little partnership ensued between Shadman and Shanto but Chase turned the game on its head. He knocked Shadman over with a beautiful in-drifter and then a reckless shot from Hridoy in the same over pushed the hosts on the back foot. Chase trapped Shanto in front in his next over to put the hosts in complete disarray.

The ball turned and gripped substantially and the slide continued for the hosts. Warrican then got rid of Litton Das and Mehidy with a couple of good deliveries. Jaker Ali (the concussion substitute for Mominul) and Nayeem Hasan have batted well but on a surface like this, you are never in as a batter. Bad light gave the hosts a breather later in the day and the umpires called stumps early. Leading by 106 with just four wickets in hand, Bangladesh's primary objective tomorrow will be stretching that past 150 - that won't be easy by any means to chase down against the trio of Taijul, Nayeem, and Mehidy. The West Indies have the upper hand but Bangladesh are in with a shot too. Join us tomorrow for what might be the final day of the Test the way it's moving. Goodbye for now...

11:09 Local Time, 05:09 GMT, 10:39 IST: A brilliant bowling performance from West Indies has enabled them to skittle Bangladesh out for a paltry total. The West Indies have to chase down 170. The visitors are in a strong position but you can't quite be sure on this surface which is turning and gripping. Skipper Roston Chase led from the front and finished with a 5-fer while Warrican was impressive once again and took a 4-fer. It was Nayeem Hasan who stood in the way of the Windies and raised his maiden fifty on a tricky surface. The young man batted with a lot of grit and determination and has given his side more than a glimmer of hope. The tail also wagged for a bit and gave good support to Nayeem. I still reckon Bangladesh are still 40-50 runs short. Their spin troika of Taijul, Nayeem, and Mehidy has to come to the party if they are to defend 169. Join us shortly for the final innings...
